source_snapshot.items: Check bootdevice unique name in BIOS setup
source_snapshot.procedure: Boot into BIOS Setup and check that the OS boot-order entry displays a unique name, for example ubuntu 22.04.
source_snapshot.criteria: The OS entry in BIOS boot order displays the unique name.
source_snapshot.script: No Master command; 10 attended/10 machine minutes; unique row/code/variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; retains interactive BIOS screen inspection by an operator.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY/MEDIUM; requires canonical UEFI label/device identity, view-only navigation, real screen evidence, no-save exit and post-boot recovery.

old_problem: The example label is not an authoritative expected value, and neither the UEFI Boot####/device-path mapping nor safe Setup entry/no-save recovery was specified. Those are project execution inputs rather than an unresolved test method.
disposition_reason: The required observation is clear and ED-06/11/15/20 permit the canonical label, boot disk/EFI mapping and console procedure as runtime project configuration. Real BIOS Setup visual evidence remains mandatory; OS-side `efibootmgr` may corroborate but cannot replace it. No random BIOS modification is allowed.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2232, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2233 / Wistron-BMC Sanity-00015-V002 / a84f193c2f176c49 was directly read from XLSX and its historical record.
Bind the exact SUT/BIOS, installed OS/version, boot disk/EFI System Partition and expected UEFI label plus Boot####/device path.
Use an approved maintenance window and known-good KVM/local console; enter Setup only through the authorized reboot procedure.
Navigate view-only and capture the complete boot-order screen with the target entry and surrounding order; no OS-side proxy can replace the rendered BIOS label.
Correlate both label and device path because a plausible label may point to the wrong disk.
Exit using the approved no-save path and prove the expected OS reaches Ready afterward.
Stop on wrong target, ambiguous/missing entry, accidental edit, lost console or boot failure; no repeated reboot or setting repair.
No reboot, BIOS entry/change, KVM action, restore, retry or DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: BIOS Setup unique OS boot-option label and device mapping
test_case.purpose: Verify on the intended BIOS Setup boot-order screen that the installed OS has the approved unique UEFI label and maps to the intended boot disk rather than a generic or wrong-device entry.
required_package: Canonical UEFI label, Boot#### and device-path/boot-disk/EFI mapping with allowed normalization
Approved KVM/local console, maintenance/reboot authorization, no-save exit and boot recovery
test_case.test_command: A qualified operator enters BIOS Setup through the approved maintenance procedure, navigates view-only to the full boot-order page, captures the approved unique OS label and its device/position, exits without saving, and proves the intended OS returns to Ready. Optional `efibootmgr -v` is corroboration only.
test_case.expected_result: The complete BIOS boot-order page shows exactly the approved unique label mapped to the intended boot device and expected position; no value changes, and no-save exit returns the intended OS to Ready.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires authentic full-screen BIOS evidence, exact label/device mapping, no-change/no-save attestation and post-exit OS Ready. OS-only text, an example label without project approval, ambiguous/wrong mapping, accidental change or failed boot is not PASS. Missing bindings blocks execution, not review.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until exact SUT, expected entry/device path, maintenance window, console and recovery are signed.
View-only BIOS navigation; do not reorder, create/delete entries, alter Secure Boot/storage/security settings or save.
Stop on any accidental edit, missing/ambiguous entry, console loss or boot failure; no automatic reboot retry.
expected_evidence: Approved label, Boot####/device path and full-order expectation
Timestamped full BIOS boot-order screenshot/video with target entry and position
Post-exit intended-OS Ready and recovery evidence
test_case.recovery: On accidental edit or ambiguity, exit without saving if safe and preserve evidence. On console or boot failure, do not loop reboots; invoke the approved console/boot-recovery owner and restore only the signed baseline.

source_conflict.reason: Items, procedure and criteria consistently require a unique BIOS-rendered OS boot label; the Ubuntu text is explicitly an example.

blocked.reason: The manual visual method is clear; exact expected label/device and maintenance bindings are supplyable.
